scenes.say: Ever wonder why your data disappears when you remove a Docker container?

scenes.label: Volumes
scenes.sub: Docker-managed storage that lives outside the container.
scenes.say: Volumes are managed by Docker and keep your data safe, even if the container goes away.

scenes.label: Bind Mounts
scenes.sub: Links a folder from your host into the container.
scenes.say: Bind mounts connect a folder on your machine directly into the container, so changes show up on both sides.
Volumes are perfect for databases and backups. Bind mounts are handy for sharing configs or code from your machine.

scenes.title: Create and use a volume
scenes.say: Here, we create a volume and use it for a database. The data sticks around, even if the container is deleted.

scenes.question: Why does data disappear after removal?
scenes.wrong: Docker never saves data by default.
scenes.right: Data in the container's writable layer is deleted when the container is removed. Use a volume or bind mount to keep it.
scenes.say: Classic interview trap: if you store data inside the container, it vanishes when the container is gone. Always use a volume or bind mount for persistence.
